source: A community-supplied poster, '10 Creative Direction Commands For Better AI Ads & Graphic Design' (M2School), contributed by the user. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material - the course teaches the five-beat UGC video ad (tools/ugc_bank.json) and the avatar/product composite (tools/static_ad_bank.json), and neither of those judges an IDEA. This bank is the first thing in the app that does. The ten commands are the poster's; the `routes`, `tiers`, `cliches` and `product_photo_tells` tables are this app's own, because a command like 'avoid safe ideas' is not checkable until somebody writes down which ideas are the safe ones.
note: The shape is tools/ugc_bank.json's `checklist` - every row declares `check` as auto or manual, and an auto row names the `rule` that evaluates it. Eight of the ten are auto, two are manual, and tools/creative_ad_lint.py downgrades any auto row whose rule it cannot actually run rather than showing it checked-but-blank. That rule is ui/views/ads.py's, stated there as: a checklist that claims to have verified something it has not is worse than no checklist. The two manual rows are the two that are genuinely unjudgeable by a regex - whether the work is directed, and whether it reads as the brand tier it claims. Recording a tier and never scoring it is deliberate.

object_vocabulary.note: A route's device is usually a scene or an object, not a person - and prompt_bank.json's shared vocabulary is written for portraits. Composed without this, the worked example produced 'realistic skin textures of a bathroom shelf', because 'realistic skin textures' is one of the eight core terms and the texture layer is half skin vocabulary. These replacements score the same two layers on surfaces instead of on faces: core hits photorealistic, real-world photography and true-to-life (three distinct keys, which is what realism_lint.REQUIRED_HITS asks of core), and texture hits surface detail, tactile and imperfection (two needed). A route carrying a person sets "has_person": true and keeps the portrait vocabulary. tools/build_static_ad.py's studio mode has the same wart and is deliberately left alone here - changing it is a separate decision about an existing, tested tool.

commands.label: Start with a human insight
commands.asks: What is true about the person, before the product exists?
commands.why: An ad built on a product feature can only ever say what the thing is. An ad built on an insight says something the viewer already believes and has never heard out loud, which is the only reason a stranger keeps watching. The test is whether the sentence survives deleting the product from it.
commands.example: You do not want a cleaner house. You want ten minutes where nobody needs anything from you.

commands.label: Build from a strategic idea
commands.asks: What is the one thought the whole campaign is arguing?
commands.why: The insight is what is true; the idea is what you are going to DO about it, and they are not the same sentence. Restating the insight here is the commonest failure - it feels like progress and leaves the campaign with no argument, so every route ends up illustrating the same observation instead of advancing a claim.
commands.example: Sell the ten minutes, not the clean house - position the product as time returned rather than work done.

commands.label: Think like a creative director
commands.asks: Is this directed, or merely described?
commands.why: The difference between a brief and a photograph is a thousand decisions nothing in a prompt can make for you - what is held back, what is out of focus, what the frame refuses to show. No linter can see whether those decisions were made. This row stays yours on purpose, and it is the row most worth arguing about.
commands.example: Would a director change one thing here, or sign it off as-is?

commands.label: Make the product feel necessary
commands.asks: Does the idea collapse if you remove the product?
commands.why: The sharpest test in the framework, and mechanically checkable: if the product only appears in the SETTING - on a shelf, in a hand, on the counter - then the idea would work just as well for a competitor, and you have made an ad for the category. The product has to be load-bearing in the visual device itself.
commands.example: The device IS the product doing its job, not a scene with the product standing in it.

commands.label: Avoid safe ideas
commands.asks: Has this exact image been made ten thousand times?
commands.why: Generative models are trained on the safe idea - ask for creativity and you get the median of everything ever tagged 'advertising'. `cliches` is the banned-trope list this row checks, applied to IDEAS exactly as prompt_bank.json's `banned` is applied to realism vocabulary, and matched through realism_lint.find_terms() so that ruling a trope OUT never trips it.
commands.example: No lightbulb moment, no team high-fiving, no splash on a white background.

commands.label: Design the visual hierarchy
commands.asks: What does the eye hit first, second, third?
commands.why: A layout where everything is loud has no hierarchy, and the viewer leaves before deciding what to look at. This is the row tools/typography_bank.json exists to serve: it needs a type zone, a reading order, and a dominance that does not contradict its own ratio - build_typography.py refuses that contradiction by name rather than quietly picking one.
commands.example: Image leads, headline upper-left, logo quiet in the corner, read in that order.

commands.label: Use premium brand logic
commands.asks: Does this look like the tier it is priced at?
commands.why: Tier is carried by restraint, negative space, and what is left out - and none of those is countable. A linter that scored this would be scoring word choice, not the work, so the chosen `tier` is recorded and shown beside the gate and never scored. It is here to be argued with, not passed.
commands.example: Luxury subtracts. If the frame is busy, the tier is wrong whatever the price is.

commands.label: Push beyond normal product photos
commands.asks: Is this a photograph OF the product, or an idea the product is in?
commands.why: The command that most directly contradicts what this app could already do: tools/static_ad_bank.json's two modes are both product photos - one on a clean background, one in a pair of hands. This row literally checks that the route's device is not one of them, using `product_photo_tells` plus the mode vocabulary read from that bank, so it cannot drift away from what those modes actually are.
commands.example: Not the bottle lit well. The thing the bottle makes possible, with the bottle load-bearing in it.

commands.label: Explore multiple creative routes
commands.asks: Have you made more than one, and are they actually different?
commands.why: One route is not a choice, it is the first thing you thought of. Two routes from the same territory are also not a choice - they are one idea photographed twice - so this row counts DISTINCT territories rather than shots. That is why `routes` in this bank is a table of territories and a route instance names one.
commands.example: Two or more routes, each from a different territory, each with its own device.

commands.label: Critique and improve until campaign-ready
commands.asks: Is every other row satisfied, including the ones only you can judge?
commands.why: The only row that can say 'ready', and it cannot say it while a manual row is untouched. That is the whole reason the manual half is not decoration: an honest checklist has to let the unjudgeable rows block the verdict, or they are ornaments. It also re-checks that every composed route still clears realism_lint at 8/8 with nothing banned - a brilliant idea that does not render is not campaign-ready either.
commands.example: Every auto row green, both manual rows ticked by a human, every route 8/8.

tiers.note: This app's first brand-tier axis. Recorded on a route and shown beside the gate; never scored - see command 7.
tiers.mass: Speaks plainly and fast. Busy is allowed, because the job is to be understood at a glance by someone who was not looking.
tiers.premium: One idea, generous space, nothing shouted. Most of the work is deciding what to leave out.
tiers.luxury: Subtraction as the whole strategy. The product may be small, late, or barely lit; the restraint IS the claim.

routes.note: Creative TERRITORIES - the kinds of idea, not the ideas. A route instance is {key, name, rationale, device, tier}: `key` names the territory, `device` is the visual idea itself (the thing that is not a product photo), and `rationale` is why this territory suits this insight. Command 9 counts distinct territories, so two routes sharing a key are one route.

demonstration.label: Demonstration
demonstration.asks: Show the product doing its job, but as visual proof rather than a how-to.
demonstration.example_device: the same white shirt photographed after ten washes and after one hundred, side by side, indistinguishable

exaggerated-consequence.label: Exaggerated consequence
exaggerated-consequence.asks: Follow the problem to an absurd but internally logical end.
exaggerated-consequence.example_device: a hallway where every surface is a laundry pile, and one clear path worn through it

absence.label: Absence
absence.asks: Show the world the product is missing from, and let the gap do the arguing.
absence.example_device: a bathroom shelf with a single clean ring in the dust where the bottle used to stand

juxtaposition.label: Juxtaposition
juxtaposition.asks: Put two unlike things in one frame so the viewer does the comparison.
juxtaposition.example_device: a surgeon's instrument tray and a baby's changing table, shot identically

personification.label: Personification
personification.asks: Give the problem or the product a character and a motive.
personification.example_device: the stain treated as a house guest who will not leave, photographed as a portrait

transformation.label: Transformation
transformation.asks: Show the change itself - without the split-screen, which is on the cliche list.
transformation.example_device: one continuous surface that is worn at one end and new at the other, with no seam

scale-shift.label: Scale shift
scale-shift.asks: Photograph the product or the problem at entirely the wrong size.
scale-shift.example_device: a single fibre of the fabric at architectural scale, walked through like a canyon

ritual.label: Ritual
ritual.asks: Find the small repeated act the product already belongs to.
ritual.example_device: the same fifteen seconds at the sink, every night for a year, in one frame

cliches.note: The banned-trope list for command 5, applied to IDEAS the way prompt_bank.json's `banned` is applied to realism vocabulary. Matched through realism_lint.find_terms(), which is negation-aware, so a brief that says 'no sunset silhouette' rules the trope out rather than tripping on it. Phrases, not single words: a single word would make whole categories of legitimate idea unwritable.
terms: climbing a mountain to plant a flag

product_photo_tells.note: For command 8. A device containing one of these is a product photograph wearing the word 'device', which is exactly what the command says to push past. Read alongside the two modes in tools/static_ad_bank.json rather than instead of them, so this list cannot drift away from what those modes are.
terms: holding the product toward the camera
